study_id: Ozcan et al. - 2022 - Artificial intelligence-derived cardiac ageing is associated with cardiac events post-heart transpla

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study involves adult heart transplant recipients, uses a convolutional neural network (non‑linear AI) to predict ECG‑derived age, and evaluates post‑transplant survival/MACE outcomes; it is a peer‑reviewed observational cohort published after 2018.

identification_methods.Setting: Single-center retrospective cohort at Mayo Clinic, Rochester, MN
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective single-centre cohort using Mayo HTx database with prospective data collection
identification_methods.Address: 200 First Street SW, Rochester, MN 55902, USA
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Mayo Clinic heart transplantation database (prospective HTx registry)
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Consecutive heart transplant patients with available pre- and post‑transplant ECGs; 540 analyzed
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Convolutional neural network (CNN) built in Keras/TensorFlow
identification_methods.Input Variables: Raw 12‑lead ECG signals (averaged pre‑ and post‑transplant), recipient and donor ages, clinical covariates for multivariable models
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Average ECG age calculated from ECGs within 1 year before and after transplant; Cox proportional hazards models used for outcome analysis

population.Inclusion criteria: Consecutive cardiac transplant patients who underwent heart transplantation at Mayo Clinic between 1990 and 2018
population.Population Notes: Retrospective single‑centre cohort study using a prospective HTx database; analyses performed on patients with available pre‑ and post‑transplant ECG data

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: Convolutional neural network AI-ECG age algorithm
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Average ECG ages within 1 year before and after transplantation used as pre- and post-transplant values
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Algorithm applied without additional training; originally trained on >770,000 ECGs using raw 12-lead signals and chronological age as label
interventions_outcomes.Reported outcomes in study: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) – composite of coronary revascularization, heart failure hospitalization, re‑transplantation, and all‑cause mortality
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: MACE defined as any incident of the listed events; also reported individual components separately
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Increase in ECG age post‑transplant associated with higher risk of MACE (adjusted HR 1.58, 95% CI 1.18–2.10, p=0.002)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported against: Patients with decrease in ECG age post‑transplant (ΔECG age < 0)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reported as: Hazard ratio (HR) from Cox proportional hazards model
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All heart transplant recipients with available ECG data (n=540)
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Hazard ratio derived from multivariable Cox proportional hazards model adjusting for recipient age, donor age, sex, hypertension, diabetes, ischemic cardiomyopathy, CAV grade, HDL‑C, triglycerides, and sirolimus conversion
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Patients with increased ECG age after transplant had significantly higher risk of MACE even after adjustment for confounders
